clue.text: Serious measure — key workers are in the dark on this

definitions.text: workers are in the dark on this

parts.note: a grave matter is a serious one
a yard is a unit of measure of length
the shift key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone takes a weighty step, while the key workers are left uninformed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the dark' reads as 'uninformed', but the definition means it literally: these workers do their jobs through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The overnight work period, typically midnight to early morning, is staffed by people labouring through the hours of darkness.

clue.text: What David achieved with good fortune protecting one colonist

indicators.note: the good fortune pieces wrap around the colonist as a guard would

parts.note: making a killing means winning a fortune
I is the Roman numeral for one
ants live in colonies, so an ant is a colonist

explanation.surface: David's victory is put down to luck, with a lone settler under protection.
explanation.walkthrough: David felled Goliath, the original underdog triumph; in sport the term means a minor team beating a mighty one.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaying the giant Goliath is the biblical archetype of an underdog toppling a far stronger opponent.

clue.text: Gold plate shows this, turning up tool

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a British number plate shows a reg, the registration mark

explanation.surface: Gold plating reveals some implement as it flips over.
explanation.walkthrough: A UK car registration plate is called a reg (number) plate; 'turning up' turns REG to GER.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a boring implement, a drill with a helical bit for making holes in wood or earth.

clue.text: Agreed working to fix rug was a bugger!

indicators.note: the rug is fixed into the reworked letters, set inside them
the letters of agreed are at work, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig or toupee

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to fix a rug, which turned out to be a real pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the first word and 'to fix' sets the rug inside. 'bugger' is not an insult: it is someone planting a bug, an eavesdropper.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is to eavesdrop secretly, just as someone using a listening bug would overhear private talk.

clue.text: Miss America is alluring, Republican's admitted

indicators.note: the Republican is let in, placed within the other pieces

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
hot means sexy or alluring

explanation.surface: A beauty queen, Miss America, is so attractive that a Republican lets her in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a beauty-pageant title but is the definition: a stroke that misses the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or cricket, a swing that fails to connect with the ball entirely is a whiff or miss.

clue.text: Conservative perhaps lying over the European disaster

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the pieces are flipped and read upwards

parts.note: abed is where one may be lying, in bed
le is French for the, a European language's article

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's possible falsehoods about Europe end in catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' suggests dishonesty but means lying down; 'over' turns CABED into DEBAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating collapse or fiasco, a synonym for a calamity.

clue.text: We hear this guy runs his tongue over part of ear

indicators.note: signals that the words are said aloud and the spelling follows the sound

parts.words: this guy runs his tongue over
parts.note: he (this guy) licks, said aloud as two words

explanation.surface: We're told a man is licking part of someone's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: HE LICKS, spoken, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The helix is the curved outer rim of the external ear, named for its spiral shape.

clue.text: Making grooves in material, using blades

parts.note: fur is an animal-pelt material used in clothing
oars have blades, so rowing is using blades

explanation.surface: Someone cuts grooves into fabric with knives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blades' looks like knives but means the flat ends of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: To furrow is to plough channels or wrinkle, so furrowing is cutting long trenches into a surface.

clue.text: Needle one fishes out of lake

indicators.note: the lake is taken out of the fisher, leaving the rest

parts.note: an angler is one who fishes

explanation.surface: A fisherman pulls a needle out of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' is a verb here: to provoke or irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to goad them, which is to provoke their annoyance or rage.

clue.text: Blair cracking tedious, off-colour jokes, say

indicators.note: Blair is cracked up and broken into a new order of letters

parts.note: dry means dull or tedious

explanation.surface: Tony Blair cracks boring, slightly risqué jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like joke-telling, but it is the signal to break up the former prime minister's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribaldry is coarse, vulgar humour, of which smutty jokes are one example, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Scrapper's initial boost when wrestling

definitions.note: a scrapper here is one who scraps, abolishes, something

indicators.note: the letters wrestle and tumble into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fighter gets an early lift during a wrestling bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapper' suggests a fighter, fitting the wrestling; it means someone who scraps a law or practice.
explanation.definitionFit: An abolitionist campaigns to do away with something, historically slavery, so is one who scraps it.

clue.text: Dirty shirt, short and tight

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order
the word and is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before shortening

explanation.surface: A shirt that's grubby, too small and too snug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims AND to AN; 'tight' (drunk) shuffles SHIRT with AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to dull or stain a surface, and to dirty something is likewise to soil it.

clue.text: After firm kiss, groom's dandy

indicators.note: the kiss is placed after the firm in the answer

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
X is the conventional symbol for a kiss
to comb hair is to groom it; groom's here is groom is

explanation.surface: After a firm kiss at the wedding, the groom proves a fop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like the bridegroom but is a verb, to tidy hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain, showy man preoccupied with appearance, much like a fop.

clue.text: Sweet stuff husband's culled from Chinese text

indicators.note: the husband is removed from the text, culled out of it

parts.note: the I Ching is a classic ancient Chinese divination text
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband's sweets were cut out of a Chinese book.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread on cakes, a confection of the sweet variety.

clue.text: Setter's run in mire and grease, flipping mess!

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves; setter's is setter is, I'm

indicators.note: the run is placed inside the mire

parts.note: a bog is a mire or swamp
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the grease is flipped over and read the other way

parts.note: oil is a lubricant, grease

explanation.surface: The setter is running through mud and grease: what a mess!
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' doubles as a mild exclamation; it reverses OIL to LIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, embarrassing tangle of affairs, so a complicated situation.

clue.text: Time to study utilitarianism, but it's a grind

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill was the leading philosopher of utilitarianism

explanation.surface: A student finds studying utilitarian philosophy tediously hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read' for study is British university usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a figurative term for monotonous, wearisome routine work, i.e. a drudge.

clue.text: Hunk of stewed boar meat with date on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the date sits above the rest
stewed food is cooked down, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A chunk of boar casserole with a date on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunk' looks like a chunk of meat but means an attractive man.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is a very handsome man, just as a hunk is a muscular, attractive fellow.

clue.text: Touring India freely, Bill's worried about a drive

indicators.note: the worried Bill goes round the freely arranged India
worried letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: Bill's here is Bill is, giving the name Bill

indicators.note: the letters move freely, rearranged

explanation.surface: Bill frets as he roams India without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' is not a car trip: it is the sex drive, the libido.
explanation.definitionFit: Libidinal means relating to the libido, the psychological sex drive or instinctual desire.

clue.text: Very small number — very little, minus one million

indicators.note: minus means the letters for one million are taken away

parts.note: minimal means very little
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tiny number, almost nothing, less a million.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal sum is a token one, so slight as to be negligible, which is a synonym sense of tiny.

clue.text: African runner's go in flash car

indicators.note: the go is placed inside the car

parts.note: a limo is a flashy, luxurious car
a pop is a go or try

explanation.surface: An African sprinter takes a turn in a fancy car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; in crosswords a runner is often a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Limpopo is a major river of southern Africa, and rivers run, hence the cryptic label.

clue.text: Said what diner did, a curvy figure

indicators.note: signals the word is spoken and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a diner ate

explanation.surface: Someone describes a meal, then a shapely body.
explanation.definitionFit: The numeral 8 is formed of two loops, so it is a figure made entirely of curves.

clue.text: Hip backing band in Japan? I'm not sure this is metal

indicators.note: the word for hip is backed, read in reverse

parts.note: in means hip or fashionable
an obi is the sash worn with a Japanese kimono
um is a hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: A trendy band touring Japan: unsure if they play metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a music group, fitting 'metal', but it is a sash.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobium is a grey transition-metal element, atomic number 41.

clue.text: Roman pair squeezing a medic's feet

indicators.note: the Roman pair squeezes the other pieces between them

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Two Romans pinch a doctor's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' are metrical feet in poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi, plural of iambus, are units of verse rhythm, each an unstressed then stressed syllable.

clue.text: It helps to recall troops, having gathered round outside

indicators.note: gathered and round go outside the troops, around them

parts.note: to meet is to gather, so met is gathered
men are troops or soldiers
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A souvenir from troops who once assembled in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake kept as a reminder of a person or event.

clue.text: Partridge about to seize unknown antelope

indicators.note: the reversed name grabs the unknown and holds it inside
about means the name is turned round

parts.note: Alan Partridge is a British TV comedy character
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A partridge (the bird) is about to catch a mystery antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: Partridge is not the bird but Alan Partridge, Steve Coogan's hapless British broadcaster character.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Maybe Joaquin's steps following hobbling soldier

parts.note: a lame person hobbles
an NCO is a non-commissioned officer, a soldier

explanation.surface: Joaquin dances after a limping soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Joaquín Cortés is a famous Spanish dancer of this style.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the Spanish dance form for which the dancer Joaquín Cortés is renowned.

clue.text: Arab statesman soon to make a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: in a mo means soon

explanation.surface: An Arab politician is about to return to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' fits the surface's politics but here is a person of a state, i.e. a national.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Oman, the Arab state on the Arabian peninsula, is a 'statesman' cryptically.

clue.text: Tory in party pamphlet shows what binds us all

indicators.note: the Tory goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering
a tract is a short pamphlet
CON is short for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative at a party hands out a leaflet about what unites us.
explanation.definitionFit: The social contract is the implicit agreement among members of a society that underpins cooperation.
